commits.messageBody:
…endencies

A user opens a shell in the workspace the agent works in, from the dock, on
desktop and web, on any runtime backend. The kit was a draft with seven
listed blockers; this closes them.

Host seam: `HostExtensionServices.loadDependency(packageName)` resolves a
module from Tau's own npm dependencies, the way `loadRuntimeExtension`
already does for Pi extensions. A bundled kit's host half runs from a cache
file under userData, from which `createRequire` cannot see the app's
`node_modules`, and node-pty finds its `spawn-helper` beside its own binary
only where npm put it, so bundling is not an option either. The member needs
no permission (an in-process package could reach the module anyway) and is
denied in a worker like every live object. API version 1.7.0; the kits
distribution requires it.

Terminal Kit:
- pty sessions filed under the workspace the host has open; a thread's own
  worktree is where its shell starts when the thread is open. Capacity
  counts by that root, not by the client's string.
- terminals die with the workspace: `beforeWorkspace` names the root the
  host moves to, and every shell of another root is closed then. They
  survive a client reload (replay by byte offset, no double drawing) and a
  thread's runtime closing.
- an exited shell stays listed with its exit code until the user closes or
  restarts it; `restart` puts a fresh shell in the same place under a new
  id, so a client redraws from zero. Killing a running shell and dropping
  an ended one are the same command.
- the panel groups terminals by the thread on screen and marks the ones
  running in another thread instead of killing them; xterm takes its colors
  from the workbench tokens and is rebuilt only when the session changes,
  not on every resize.
- Windows keeps `ComSpec` instead of falling back to /bin/sh.
- tests: host round trip (open, write, resize, replay, exit, restart, kill),
  workspace close, capacity, missing node-pty, disposal; panel with a fake
  host (grouping, exit and restart, close, refusal); output reconciliation;
  the kit in the lifecycle and profile checks; the seam's name validation.
- xterm moves to devDependencies: it is bundled into the kit's desktop half.

Verified in the isolated instance: a real zsh under node-pty prints what was
typed, `exit 5` shows in the status and Restart opens a fresh prompt, a
renderer reload replays the scrollback, and opening a new thread marks the
first thread's terminal as running elsewhere.
